text:
sara: heads-up — i'm prototyping a new synth traffic generator called 'traffic orchestra' to better stress long-tail latency and kernel-selection edgecases. goal: apples-to-apples runs for batching/kernel heuristics + kv-warmup states.

mike: love the name. what's different from current loadgen?

sara: two things: 1) deterministic QPS ramps with configurable microbursts (we'll param p99 shaping), 2) explicit kv-cache state machine (cold/warm/hot) so we can compare runs with identical cache distributions.

alex: for kernels we need identical model bits: same model SHA, same quantization flags. otherwise noisy. also we should pin GRADIO env flags that affect aten kernels.

jen: +1. also include a run where batching is forced off (single-token batching) to measure kernel throughput vs. batching gains. small runs first, then scale.

kevin: can we add a replay mode that feeds recorded request lengths/QPS from prod for one-hour windows? that'll help verify that synth shapes actually map to real tail events.

sara: yes — replay mode planned. two modes: synthetic-config (ramp shapes, burst density, tail exponent) and replay-file (CSV of ts, prompt_len, user_id_hash). both should feed same harness.

mike: how do we specify microburst? e.g., spike of 300% for 2s every 30s?

sara: config snippet:
```json
{
  "base_qps": 100,
  "ramp": { "type": "linear", "duration_s": 600 },
  "microbursts": [ { "rate_multiplier": 3, "duration_s": 2, "interval_s": 30 } ],
  "tail_shape": { "type": "pareto", "alpha": 2.5 }
}
```

alex: nice. make sure the generator supports jittered interval so spikes aren't perfectly periodic — that hides timing artifacts in autoscaling.

jen: for KV warmup states, propose: cold (no cache), partial-warm (50% prefix coverage), hot (95%). we should instrument cache hit histogram in the runtime and export as prometheus labels so we can verify target.

kevin: agree. also log per-request kernel selection and batch-size used so we can correlate p99 regressions with kernel path.

perf-bot: quick note: created perf test job template traffic-orchestra:v1 — uses dedicated infra with pinned model sha abc123, 4xGPUs, 30m warmup.

mike: what's the plan for apples-to-apples? multiple runs back-to-back with only one variable changed?

sara: yes. baseline-run (current batching heuristics + kernel selector), then ablated-run (disable kv-cache), then kernel-force-run (force kernel X), then autobatch-tuned-run. each run same seed + same replay file when applicable.

jen: and record system-level counters: NVML GPU utilization, kernel-time slices from profiling, per-batch-latency, and context-switch rates. I can add a small wrapper to push these into the perf dashboard.

alex: watch out for startup effects — kernel JITs and allocator warmups. include a 10m discard window and only compute stats after.

sara: will do. i also want an experimental mode that gradually shifts kv-state during the run (simulate users activating prefixes) — that'll help verify smoothing heuristics for kv-eviction.

kevin: how do we validate the generator itself?

sara: validation plan: 1) unit tests for ramp math and burst scheduling, 2) run with synthetic deterministic seed and assert event timestamps, 3) replay recorded prod window and compare distribution histograms (latency, prompt_len, interarrival).

perf-bot: FYI — perf harness now collects per-request metadata under label traffic_orchestra=true; saved to s3://perf-artifacts/traffic-orchestra/1749998888/

mike: any blockers?

sara: small: need a short-lived SRE quota bump for parallel runs. filing ticket now. otherwise i'll push a PR with generator + sample configs tomorrow.

jen: once PR is up, can run a baseline with me and alex watching metrics. i want to validate p50/p95/p99 shifts when we toggle batching heuristics.

alex: i'll add a kernel-level tracer to capture selection decisions per-batch. might add a heatmap export.

kevin: thanks all. excited to see if our long-tail shaping surfaces the regression we saw last week. :crossed_fingers:

sara: thanks — i'll post the PR link and perf job id once queued.
